title: Novus Loyalty Ltd - 544735 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Novus Loyalty FY26 revenue rose about 22% to ~127 Cr, with PAT of ~9.28 Cr (7.29% margin) in its first results call after its 25 March 2026 listing.
summary.overview: Novus Loyalty, a B2B2C loyalty and engagement technology company, reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about 127 Cr, up roughly 22% YoY. EBITDA was about 12.33 Cr (9.68% margin) and PAT about 9.28 Cr (7.29% margin), with management citing PAT growth of about 150% and EBITDA growth of about 120%. Management attributed margin improvement to programs maturing (redemptions rising in years 2 to 3) and a shift toward technology and merchant-promotion revenue, which carry no direct procurement cost. Management guided to growth above 20% in FY27 and to international revenue at least doubling, but gave no formal numerical guidance, and the call was largely promotional with limited hard data.

financial_highlights.change: listed 25 March 2026; no proceeds utilised in FY26

segments.name: Technology
segments.commentary: Enterprise platform set-up fee and the first revenue line to open with a client; management says it carries no direct cost and is the main focus. Cited Central Bank order worth 88 Cr (via GeM) and Bank of Abyssinia technology revenue of about 4 Cr.

segments.name: Redemption
segments.commentary: Second revenue line, opening after technology in BFSI programs; carries a direct procurement cost. Management cited a client where redeeming customers rose from about 10,000 to 10 lakh within 10 months.

segments.name: Merchant promotions
segments.commentary: Merchants fund accelerated campaigns and pay affiliate commissions, which management said run at about 8-10% of tracked spend, of which part is passed to customers. Described as a higher-margin line with no direct cost.

segments.name: Digital vouchers
segments.commentary: Fourth line; vouchers sourced partly from vendors such as Gyftr. Carries direct procurement cost. Management said the voucher line is about 5% of Gyftr's business in its comparison.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 growth will be above 20%, but gave no revenue number.

International revenue to at least double from about 3.3 Cr in FY26, 'if not triple'. Management cited about 5 Cr for FY27 and more than 6 Cr in one answer, then 'close to 10' / 'more than 10' for FY27-28, which is internally inconsistent.
Margins expected to rise from current levels as the mix shifts toward technology and merchant promotion.
IPO proceeds planned as about 11-12 Cr for sales and business development (about half in FY27), about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.
Bank accounts onboarded recently, such as Central Bank, are expected to reach peak levels in FY27, which management said could increase numbers by 100%.
capex_capacity: Planned UAE wholly owned subsidiary, expected to be finalised in about a month; physical presence to serve MENA clients.
Two partners onboarded in Africa, with workshops started; Bank of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) order is the first such contract.

Planned acquisition of a small marketing agency or digital agency in the US and Australia, targeted this year or next, subject to finding the right candidate. Management also cited a PPI licence as a possible acquisition target.
Hiring additional sales staff in India for channel partner and corporate loyalty programs; management said BFSI needs no extra staff.
Platform scales from 10,000 to 100 million customers, with SaaS launch in about 2-3 weeks and on-premise deployment for banks.
demand_pricing: Over 100 enterprise customers and more than 4 crore end-customers on the platform; about 50 crore transactions processed per month; about 80 employees.
Clients include NPCI (since 2019), Central Bank, IDBI, Bank of Maharashtra, Equitas Bank, Sparkle Bank (Nigeria), PRYPCO (DAMAC) and NovaDisk (healthcare, 3 countries).
Contracts run 3-5 years with 3-5 year renewals (6-10 year total tenure). Programs typically mature in year 3, and management said margins rise over the program life.
Competition: management named Salesforce and other large loyalty players in the Bank of Abyssinia tender; said its platform processes transactions in 8 hours versus 24 hours for others.
Redemption rates in Indian bank programs are about 10%, against 45-50% in the US and Australia, which management cited as upside.
Management said seasonality has a 5-10% effect, mainly around September-October festive months.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth exceed 20% in FY27, and what revenue is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would be 'more than' 20% and that IPO-funded sales and international expansion would grow the business faster than FY26, but gave no revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~10% margins sustainable, or were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would increase from current levels as technology and merchant promotion revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: How will IPO proceeds be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately 11-12 Cr for business development and sales, about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Does Novus keep breakage on expired points, and what about gift points?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Novus is B2B2C and breakage goes to the bank client; it does not hold a PPI licence, so it cannot keep breakage. Management said Indian bank points expiry is about 7-10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international revenue mix and reseller economics?
qa_highlights.answer: International revenue was about 2.6% of FY26 revenue (about 3.3 Cr). Resellers take about 15-30% of the deal value depending on local support needs, and Novus retains IP ownership.

qa_highlights.question: How does Novus compare with Zaggle and Gyftr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Zaggle focuses on spend management and employee rewards, which are about 5-10% of Novus's business. Gyftr is a voucher vendor to Novus, not a loyalty competitor.

risks_watch: Growth depends on the timing of program maturity and on contract wins, including government/GeM tenders that management said can be cancelled or uneven (Canara order cancelled).
International expansion relies on partners, resellers and a planned US/Australia acquisition, with reseller margins of 15-30% and a licence-dependent PPI plan that is not yet in place.
The FY27 international revenue guidance is internally inconsistent (about 5 Cr, then more than 6 Cr, then 10 Cr or more), so the number needs confirmation.
Concentration in BFSI and a few large bank and government clients; redemption-driven revenue carries direct procurement cost.
Use of IPO proceeds (about 60 Cr raised) has not yet been reported; watch quarterly deployment and the outcome of the planned acquisition.
Management did not give FY26 comparatives in detail; the EBITDA and PAT growth figures (120%, 150%) are management's approximations.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive, with heavy forward-looking claims on international growth, margins and FY27 growth. Answers on specific numbers (FY27 revenue, acquisition timing, international mix) were loose or inconsistent, and the call relied on narrative more than data.
key_quotes: So, we are, like, about our PAT is, like, almost 150% increase, EBITDA is about 120% increase, revenue is 22% increase, and these numbers are gonna go better, over time.
Margins will increase from where they are right now.
We are aggressive in finding the right company, 100%. We are actively looking.
Technology revenue is more, so one of the key focus gonna be the technology revenue.

adds.what: Platform scale-up from 10,000 to 100 million customers (software capacity, not physical plant)

growth.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth above 20% (no number given), India growth 15-20%, and international revenue to at least double from about 3.3 Cr, backed by the Central Bank order (88 Cr via GeM), Bank of Abyssinia contract, and a SaaS launch in 2-3 weeks, but with no formal numerical guidance and internally inconsistent international targets.
